subject: Fintegro private connectivity + SDK auth: post-call playbook
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice@fintegro.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Fintegro onramp — connectivity & SDK auth

Alice — thanks for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have alignment. High-level ask: Fintegro wants a private onramp for PII workloads using Redwood Private with predictable latency and no internet egress.

What we covered (short):
- Target: Migrate inference for transaction enrichment to Redwood Private (initially 15 req/s, 200 token avg).
- Connectivity model: Customer-managed VPC with interface endpoint (our recommended path) vs. transit Peering.
- Auth: SDK + short-lived service tokens; option for mTLS for SecOps.
- Structured output: tool-calling for normalization + embeddings + reranker for retrieval.
- Compliance: SOC2 evidence required by Aug 2.

Information we need from Fintegro to scope work: (please reply inline)
1) Preferred private connectivity: VPC Endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) or VPC Peering/Transit?
2) Egress policy: do you allow outbound to our control plane (api.redwood-inference.com) via NAT or do you need fully private control plane?
3) IP allowlist and CIDR ranges for your consumer hosts (dev/test/prod).
4) DNS and split-horizon requirements (do you host private DNS for endpoints?).
5) Cert management: do you require customer-provided client certs / CA for mTLS or will you use ACM?
6) SOC2/Legal POC: primary contact and any standard NDA requirements.

Attachments: fintegro_mvp_network_diagram.png, redwood_private_onramp_checklist.pdf (first-pass checklist).

Proposed next steps (owners & timeline):
- Alice/Fintegro: answer Q1–Q5 by Mon 7/24 (Alice + SecOps).
- Redwood (Irene): produce configuration playbook and sample cURL/mTLS config by Tue 7/25.
- Redwood (Marissa): share rollout + SLA summary and Ops contact by Tue 7/25.
- Schedule technical deep-dive (60m) wk of 7/31 — propose Tue 7/31 10am PT.

If that looks good, we’ll draft a short integration playbook and a test account for your engineers.

Thanks,
Ben

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Fintegro onramp — connectivity & SDK auth

Thanks Ben — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side and some answers:

Q1: Prefer AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoint) to start — peering introduces cross-account routing complexity we want to avoid.
Q2: We want no internet egress from prod inference. Control plane traffic can go over our existing NAT for now, but we'd prefer PrivateLink to a regional control-plane endpoint long term.
Q3: IP ranges: prod 10.4.0.0/20, staging 10.8.16.0/20. We will produce full allowlist in the next email.
Q4: Yes, we operate split-horizon DNS via Route 53 Resolver endpoints. Private DNS is required for hostnames.
Q5: SecOps prefers customer-provided client certs signed by our PKI for mTLS (rotation every 90 days). We use HashiCorp Vault for cert lifecycle.

SOC2 evidence: attaching the initial questionnaire (fintegro-soc2-qa.xlsx). Primary SecOps contact is secops@fintegro.com (on cc).

One question: for the embeddings + reranker flow you mentioned, where would the embeddings be stored — in our VPC (S3) or in Redwood-managed storage? We have contractual constraints about storing PII outside our VPC.

We can do the deep-dive Tue 7/31 10am PT, that works.

Regards,
Alice Park
Head of Product, Fintegro
alice@fintegro.com

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice@fintegro.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 Jul 2028 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Fintegro onramp — connectivity & SDK auth (technical answers)

Hi Alice — thanks for the answers and the SOC2 worksheet. Below are direct responses and a short technical playbook for the items you brought up.

1) Connectivity: PrivateLink (interface VPC endpoint) is the cleanest path for your constraint of no cross-account peering complexity. We support an interface endpoint in each region; traffic to the inference runtime (data plane) flows over the endpoint and never traverses public internet. Control-plane operations (model selection/rollouts) can be proxied through the same endpoint or via a dedicated control-plane private endpoint. We will provide CloudFormation snippets for the endpoint service and an example endpoint ENI policy.

2) Egress/Control plane: For fully private control-plane connectivity, we can stand up a regional private control-plane endpoint reachable via PrivateLink. Short-term, using your NAT for control plane calls is supported but you should confirm internal firewall rules allow outbound to 10.0.0.0/16 (our control-plane overlay) or we can provide dedicated IPs to allowlist.

3) DNS: We support private DNS mapping for the endpoint hostname (e.g., private-api.redwood-inference.internal). With Route 53 Resolver, you can configure conditional forwarding to make the endpoint hostname resolve to the interface ENI IP. We'll include recommended /etc/hosts fallback for early testing.

4) mTLS & cert rotation: We support client-side mTLS using customer-provided certs. Options:
  - Customer-provided certs: you upload client cert + chain to our onboarding portal; we validate on connect and enforce CN/SAN restrictions.
  - ACME/ACM: we can integrate with ACM for certs if you prefer managed certs.
Rotation: Redwood supports cert rotation via an automated short-lived credential exchange: client certs can be rotated and we accept certs issued by your CA as long as the chain is uploaded and pinned. We also provide a script to fetch certs from Vault (example below).

Vault fetch example (pseudo):
  curl -s \n    --header "X-Vault-Token: $VAULT_TOKEN" \n    https://vault.company/secrets/redwood/client-cert | jq -r '.data.pem' > client.pem

Then: configure SDK with --mtls-client-cert client.pem and restart the process.

5) Embeddings storage and PII: For PII constraints, we offer two options:
  - Store embeddings in your VPC: Redwood will run a small connector that pushes vectors to your S3 with server-side encryption and fine-grained IAM. Retrieval/rerank calls route back to Redwood runtime over PrivateLink for scoring.
  - Redwood-managed vector store within a private subnet of your account (deployable during Private onramp) so data never leaves your control plane.
We can default to "Store in your VPC (S3)" for compliance; will need a short IAM policy we can assume for write access.

6) Structured output & reranker: For structured tool-calling flows we suggest the following pattern for predictability and cost: prefix batching + KV prefix caching on the model side, run candidate generation in the runtime, then call your reranker hosted in your VPC via the PrivateLink endpoint for final scoring, or optionally let Redwood run the reranker if you permit vector storage in Redwood-managed private subnet. We'll include an example request/response JSON in the playbook.

Attachments: I’ve uploaded a revised playbook draft to the Drive link and attached the playbook checklist.

Next milestones (Irene / Redwood):
- 7/25: deliver CloudFormation snippets + endpoint ENI policy (Irene).
- 7/26: sample Vault -> cert rotation script + SDK mTLS example (Irene).
- 7/28: draft integration runbook with embedding-storage options & IAM minimal policy (Irene + Marissa).

Technical deep-dive Tue 7/31 10am PT — I’ll include a demo of the PrivateLink flow and an end-to-end embedding+rerank run (test account).

If you want, I can also prepare an RFC-style one-pager for your SecOps team that maps our audit logs to SOC2 controls.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com

Alice — quick ops notes from Redwood side:

- SLA & Monitoring: We can offer a 99.9% uptime SLA for Dedicated capacity once the reserved capacity contract is signed. For Private onramp we provide per-route latency/availability dashboards and token-level cost reports.
- Rollout plan (recommended):
  * Week 0: Test account + PrivateLink endpoint in staging (0–7 days)
  * Week 1: Canary traffic (1–5% prod load) + detailed error/latency tracing
  * Week 2–3: Ramp to full production and enable automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant if latency degrades.
- Owners: Marissa (Ops lead) — runbook, Irene (SE) — technical config, Ben (AE) — commercial & procurement.
- Audit logs: We will enable token-level request logs and can send them to your S3 bucket or to a third-party SIEM via our forwarder.

Irene — please include the minimal IAM policy and ENI security-group example in the playbook.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
